intended_object: The symmetric difference a ∆ b = (a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a), as in sets or generalized Boolean algebras. Inferred from the docstring and the name. The `to_dual` attribute also produces the Heyting bi-implication (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b).
explanation: The body is exactly `a \ b ⊔ b \ a`, which is the textbook definition of symmetric difference. It only assumes the operations `⊔` and `\` (the `Max` and `SDiff` classes), which is the most general setting where the formula makes sense. On sets it gives the usual (A \ B) ∪ (B \ A). In Boolean algebras it gives the usual symmetric difference (XOR), so it is not too narrow. The dual version is the standard Heyting bi-implication (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b), which matches its docstring. This is Mathlib's own canonical definition, so there is no other Mathlib declaration to cite as a counterpart.
